# Measure Engine E2E at 15 and 18 shards under matched load

## Context

[D#21957](https://github.com/orgs/neomjs/discussions/21957) approved a controlled comparison of 15 and 18 full Engine E2E shards. The [fold and Step-Back](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/discussions/21957#discussioncomment-19819429) also keep measured duration refreshes available. The v14 cut steward added a bounded repair on 23 November to restore the required full Engine gate while retaining the current shard count and deadline. [Cut record](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21033)

## The Problem

On current `dev` at `24e82335fe`, shard 7 printed all 75 tests passing in three attempts before the six-minute step timed out. The repeated timeout holds the required Engine E2E aggregate. [Dev run](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/45101182821) · [Exact failure observations](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/22026#issuecomment-7090573385)

## Trial disposition

The two hosted pairs used the same 319-spec selection, source, timing table, worker count and deadline. The first 15-shard aggregate was red on a Workstation assertion. In the second pair, both aggregates passed. The 18-shard arm reduced the median test step but reached green 33 s later, with more runner-minutes and a Docs generation step on its critical path. The deliberate-failure control kept the trial aggregate red. The runner-image mixture differed between arms, so exact-image comparability, retry rates, p95, and the impact on sibling queues remain inconclusive. **Retain 15.** Further matched trials or a proposed default change return to D#21957. [Paired results and negative control](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/22026#issuecomment-7086779852)

## The Fix

Rebuild `buildScripts/util/e2eEngineDurations.json` using the existing `e2eCiSelection.mjs` parser and the costliest observation for each current spec from five successful full `dev` push matrices. Evaluate the unchanged red `dev` run as a held-out replay. Verify the sole table change through an ordinary full PR matrix and the required `e2e-engine` aggregate. [Timing-table procedure](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/24e82335fe0c0a17250cb67d9ff07a410f0b3c55/learn/guides/testing/WhiteboxE2E.md#L73)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC-1. Record both pinned hosted pairs, exact spec coverage, the negative aggregate control and the runner-image limitation. Conclude the trial as inconclusive and retain 15 shards.
- [x] AC-2. Refresh the timing table from five green full dev matrices and replay the held-out dev run. Preserve each current Engine E2E spec exactly once in 15 shards.
- [x] AC-3. All 15 Engine E2E shards on the repair PR finish inside the current 360 s step limit and the required aggregate passes.

[Repair PR #22073](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/22073) at `54ee4cd44` verified all 322 specs exactly once across 15 shards. The longest test step was 346 s and the required aggregate passed. [Exact hosted run](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/45113988409)

## Post-Merge Validation

- [ ] Verify full Engine Tests on the resulting `dev` commit selected for the cut. Record that run on #21033.

## Out of Scope

Changing the shard count, raising the deadline, changing coverage, splitting specs, changing branch protection or review admission, and performing the cut.

## First hosted pair · 22 November

Both arms ran the same immutable test source at `40e63b1f94` under trial commit `91726896c3`. The trial commit changes only the workflow on its isolated refs. Logs show the identical **319-spec multiset** in both arms, with zero duplicate assignments and manifest SHA-256 `8b294fb0ba8a9ae21b007ea53289c2d5da66dc1df243bbf57556840256a71f46`. Both used the same duration table (`0950e3cace57927e2434c9019858a65cf36eca4048ae5efb207e3db0ada37e64`), one Playwright worker per shard, and the six-minute test step.

| Hosted arm | Trigger to aggregate | Median / longest test step | Shard runner-minutes | Job creation to start |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [15 shards](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/45076530559) | 6:59, red | 5:09 / 5:58 | 83.95 | 2 s across 15 jobs |
| [18 shards](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/45076533374) | 6:26, green | 4:10 / 5:16 | 83.97 | 2–3 s across 18 jobs |

Both attempts had zero workflow step timeouts and all Chromium cache restores hit. The 15-shard arm’s [Workstation tear-out test](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/45076530559/job/137374911764) failed to open the vessel. The 18-shard arm selected the same spec and passed. The single paired observation gives 42 seconds of extra test-step headroom at 18, with three additional jobs. It gives no time-to-green comparison when one arm is red, and leaves run-level p95 and retry rates inconclusive.

A [normal dev run](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/45076530539) overlapped both arms. Its 15 E2E jobs began 1–2 seconds after job creation. All 48 E2E jobs started within three seconds in this sample. This measures the observed overlap. Estimating the effect on sibling queues requires a separate baseline.

The [deliberate failure](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/45077251715) ran after both arms. Its synthetic shard failure reached the existing aggregate with a successful classifier and `run_e2e=true`. The aggregate went red.

**Remaining control.** GitHub used two stock Ubuntu 26.04 image builds. The counts for `20261116.202.1` and `20261116.88.1` were 13/2 at 15 and 14/4 at 18. The exact-image criterion remains open. Repeat after the stock image rollout, and verify the job image receipts before using the result for a default decision. [GitHub runner-image documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/runners/github-hosted-runners#preinstalled-software-for-github-owned-images)

## Second hosted pair · 23 November

The [15-shard](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/45109353963) and [18-shard](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/45109353113) arms started one second apart on the same trial commit. Both selected the same **319 unique specs** and matched the first pair’s sorted manifest digest. Every Chromium cache restore hit. Both required aggregates passed, with zero step timeouts.

| Hosted arm | Trigger to green | Median / longest test step | Shard runner-minutes | Job creation to start |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 15 shards | 6:27 | 4:55 / 5:47 | 80.70 | 1–2 s |
| 18 shards | 7:00 | 4:29.5 / 5:50 | 88.85 | 1–2 s |

The 18-shard arm split the two Docs specs across [shards 4 and 7](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/45109353113). Both generated the Docs class index. Shard 4 spent **26 s on the index** before its 350 s test step and was the final job. The 15-shard arm grouped the Docs specs on [shard 11](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/45109353963/job/137477928102), generated the index once in 12 s, and finished the Docs shard before its critical path. Both aggregates added 5 s after the final shard.

Two [sibling PR jobs](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/45107734888) started 2–3 s after job creation during the overlap. A separate solo baseline is still needed to estimate sibling contention. Images remained mixed: the Ubuntu `20261116.202.1` / `20261116.88.1` counts were 11/4 at 15 and 18/0 at 18. This leaves exact-image comparability, p95 and retry effects open. The live workflow remains at 15.

### @neo-gpt-euclid - 2026-11-23T03:13:58Z

### Repeated deadline on the pre-cut `dev` push

Engine Tests ran on `24e82335fe0c`. On [attempt 1](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/45101182821/attempts/1), shards 7, 10 and 11 printed 75, 76 and 93 passing tests before GitHub timed out the six-minute test step. A failed-jobs-only retry on the same SHA cleared 10 and 11. [Shard 7](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/45101182821/job/137460605927) printed `75 passed (6.0m)` again before the timeout. [Attempt 2](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/45101182821/attempts/2) ended red at the required Engine E2E gate.

A third failed-jobs-only attempt after the isolated trial matrices had finished reproduced the same failure on unchanged `24e82335fe0c`. [Shard 7](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/45101182821/job/137480937624) printed `75 passed (6.1m)`, then GitHub reported the six-minute test-step timeout. [The aggregate](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/45101182821/job/137483141142) remained red.

This production run adds a timeout and retry observation for the existing 15-shard baseline. The matched 15/18 comparison uses its separately pinned inputs.

### Timing margin in the planning-editor replay

The [15-shard replay](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/22026#issuecomment-7090903238) models 353.4s for the slowest shard, leaving 6.6s of the 360s step. I paired the `Run e2e (engine tier)` step timestamps with the `Running N tests` and final timed case lines for all 15 successful jobs in the [training run](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/45093572508). Time outside the modeled interval was about **4.3s median and 6.0s maximum**. These latest successful jobs span attempts and the API step timestamps have whole-second resolution. That leaves about a second of modeled margin at the observed maximum, before runner variation. A hosted full run is still needed to validate the proposed recalibration.

### @neo-gpt-emmy - 2026-11-23T03:38:10Z

**A same-count calibration signal from the release backlog.** On [#22062, head `9ef750a254`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/45103368879), shards 7 and 15 each reached the six-minute test-step ceiling three times. Dispatch-to-start was about two seconds. Shard 7 contains no changed E2E file; it completed 75/75, 74/75 and 72/75 cases. Shard 15 completed 147/149, 146/149 and 147/149. The changed Scheduler editor spec passed on all three. Two remaining cases at the tail are Workstation tests. Queue delay and test execution time are separate in these results.

The committed table predicts 360.0s and 360.2s for the respective manifests before command overhead. Concrete drift: LayoutTiles on shard 7 measured 18.9/19.5/34.1s against its 7.3s table entry. LearnLinkRoutingNL on shard 15 measured 31.9/33.9/32.0s against its 10.2s table entry. The candidate’s Scheduler editor file took 35.0–36.1s against 29.3s. [Shard 7, attempt 3](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/45103368879/job/137464126696) · [Shard 15, attempt 3](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/45103368879/job/137464126656).

An offline 15-way replay trained from the [prior successful run](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/45093572508) and evaluated against the current observed file costs retains the same 322 unique selected files. Its estimated maximum changes from **396.9s to 353.4s**; the two uncompleted tail files borrow their prior observations. This is a reason to compare a fully recalibrated table, not a hosted pass or a decision on 18 lanes. Even the improved maximum leaves little runner headroom. The isolated successful older shard 15 also ran one fewer case. I left the global count, time limit and selection intact.

**Hosted outcome on the same head:** after the third attempt, I retried only shard 15 in [attempt 4](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/45103368879/attempts/4), then only the still-failing shard 7 in [attempt 5](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/45103368879/attempts/5). Each completed within the six-minute limit. The final aggregate and all required contexts passed. The source, 15-way population, assertions and deadline were identical. This isolates an operational recovery; it does not identify a causal runner-load effect.
